title: A pricing dilemma
caption: Whatever the rival does, cutting price pays each firm more, so both cut and earn £6m. That is the Nash equilibrium, and it leaves both worse off than the £10m each they would earn by keeping prices high.
alt: A payoff grid for two firms choosing a high or low price: both high £10m each; A low, B high A £12m and B £4m; A high, B low A £4m and B £12m; both low £6m each. Both low is the Nash equilibrium.
description: One prices low while the other stays high: the low-price firm earns £12m and the other £4m.
Low is each firm's dominant strategy, so both price low: the Nash equilibrium, worse for both than £10m each.
